title: Sum, then clear
hints: Do every load first, through views of `%b`. Then you need two stores, and each store needs its own `after`.
The first store can go into `shrink %b 2 []`. Name the result with `%b1 = after %b ...`. The second store must go into a view of `%b1`, not of `%b`.
Load b[0] and b[1] from `%b`, `add` them, store the sum into `shrink %b 2 []`, then `%b1 = after %b %s0`. Finish with `store` of `0` into `shrink %b1 0 []` and `%b2 = after %b1 %s1`.
explain: Both loads read version `%b`, so they see the starting values. The first store writes the sum into element 2 and `after %b` names version 1. The second store writes 0 into element 0 of version 1, and its `after` names version 2, the final version. Storing the 0 first works too, as long as the loads still go through views of `%b` and each store writes into the latest version.
